newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel says economy's slowing trend has ended.
newsitem.headline: Israel says economy's slowing trend has ended.

text.p: Indicators for August and September point to a bottoming out in the slowing trend in the Israeli economy, the Central Bureau of Statistics (CBS) said on Monday.
The indicators showed an increase in imports of production inputs over the two months, after a decline in the February-July period. Imports of machinery and equipment rose in September, the CBS said.
The industrial production index rose in August at an annualised rate of four percent after rising by two-to-three percent in the April-July period.
In addition, industrial exports -- not counting diamonds and exports to the West Bank and Gaza Strip -- continued their rising trend that began in May, the CBS said.
Industrial exports briefly stabilised in February-April. Overall, merchandise exports grew at a seven percent annualised rate in September, compared with a three-to-five percent rate in March-August.

Retail sales also continued strongly, showing annualised growth of nine-to-ten percent since June. Imports of consumer durables, a related indicator, were up in July-September, after falling in the third quarter.
Meanwhile, inflation has slowed since May, the CBS said, with consumer prices rising at just a four percent annualised rate in September.
Tourist arrivals by air also showed improvement, after falling sharply in the wake of guerrilla attacks last winter, fighting in neighbouring Lebanon and the TWA jet crash in the United States.

Tourist arrivals began to pick up in August on a seasonally adjusted basis after falling in June and July. Nevertheless, the CBS noted, arrivals were 10 percent in August lower than in the year-earlier period.
